keyFindings.finding: Sparse cone worktrees (git worktree add --no-checkout + git sparse-checkout set) keep every machinery surface — registration, lease, sweep, publish, churn detector — and cut disk ~60% (0.6 GB cone vs 1.6 GB) with setup/teardown scaling with materialization; attribution stays exact because the lane remains a linked worktree of the same repo.

Exact attribution requires a per-lane index plus a per-lane tree of the same repo; the churn detector is exact only inside a real git working tree, and git has no per-writer identity for writes into a shared tree. One shared checkout cannot be made exact; the only cheaper-than-full exact form is sparse.

The 1.6 GB/lane is tracked tree materialization (85% specs/, deep-review artifact dirs), not objects: the object store (2.06 GiB in-pack) is already shared by worktrees, so object-sharing alternatives (reference/shared clones) attack nothing.
keyFindings.evidence: git ls-tree -r -l HEAD; git count-objects -vH; implementation-summary.md:106

keyFindings.finding: Shallow clones cut history not tree and add a repo boundary the sweep cannot see; reference/shared clones carry the documented corruption hazard (source-repo maintenance can prune referenced objects); partial clones require a real transport (--local ignores filters) and make the churn detector's status/hash-object trigger promisor fetches that couple lane liveness to the source path.

CoW/overlay lanes (APFS clonefile, overlayfs) win disk and lose everything else: the lane is not a git working tree, so the detector hard-fails (repo resolvable, artifact outside worktree) or fails open, the sweep cannot reclaim the dir (git worktree remove requires registration), and git index coherence breaks; clonefile is macOS/same-filesystem-only, overlayfs needs Linux + privilege.

Single worktree with per-lane write redirection was already scored 3/10 in ADR-003 (misattribution moved one level down); five of seven executor kinds reach their tree only via spawn cwd or read root, and the ADR-005 checkout watch is report-only — its legitimate place is the degrade path, where it already lives.

Per-lane sandboxed dirs with a shared object store collapse into a clone or a worktree (a dir without a git identity cannot use the store and is detector-blind); the per-lane-index + checkout-index variant recreates the wrong-tree bug because the runner's status calls read the repo default index.

git worktree move/relocation survives only under the sparse worktree: sparse state lives in the per-worktree gitdir (moves with the tree) and the self-links are relative by design; clones hold path-dependent remotes, and non-git lanes have no registration.

The sparse config trap (core.sparseCheckout leaking to the shared config and making the main checkout sparse) is real and is handled by git >= 2.37 (sparse-checkout set enables extensions.worktreeConfig and writes per-worktree); adoption residue is the repo-wide extension, which older git refuses.

resolvedQuestions.question: Which git-native materialization lever cuts the cost while keeping all machinery?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Sparse cone worktree; the cone is a superset of .opencode/, the target spec family, dispatch-named spec paths, and the seed list.

resolvedQuestions.question: What is the minimum read cone a lane needs?
resolvedQuestions.answer: .opencode/ (~253 MB) + target spec family (specs/system-deep-loop, ~356 MB) + any other dispatch-named spec path + seed paths; cone mode is include-only per directory, so granularity is family not packet.

resolvedQuestions.question: Can a non-git mechanism deliver exact attribution?
resolvedQuestions.answer: No. Exact attribution requires a per-lane index + tree of the same repo (the invariant); every non-git lane is detector-blind, hard-fails, or recreates the wrong-tree bug.

resolvedQuestions.question: Which breakage classes does each mechanism violate?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Sparse: none (inherits split-relink, relative self-links, provisioning, exact detector). Clones: sweep/lease/publish break (new repo boundary); partial clones additionally break the detector via promisor fetches. CoW/sandbox/redirection: detector, self-links (re-anchor), and reclaim break.

resolvedQuestions.question: What survives relocation and what must change in the runner?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Only the sparse worktree survives git worktree move (per-worktree gitdir carries the cone; relative self-links). Runner changes: cone-aware createLineageWorktree, per-run cone computation, minimum git >= 2.37, and a stub-executor measurement run to confirm the per-lane time saving.
